page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmc6e.26xlarge is a bare-metal, compute-optimized server type belonging to the ECS Bare Metal family. It is driven by the x86_64 architecture and features 104 dedicated virtual cores powered by Intel Xeon 8269CY processors managed via a KVM hypervisor. With 192.0 GB of system memory, the instance provides roughly 1.85 GB of RAM per vCPU, aligning with compute-intensive workload profiles that require dense processing capacity rather than expansive memory footprints.

The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage disks, necessitating external network-attached block storage for persistence and operational file systems. Network capabilities include a baseline throughput of 32 Gbps, providing substantial interconnect capacity for distributed communication. Because there are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses bundled with the instance, external network routing requires allocated elastic IP assets.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated allocation of 104 cores delivers predictable execution without hypervisor overhead or multitenancy resource contention. The low memory-to-vCPU ratio maximizes core-per-chassis utilization for parallel compute workloads. Tradeoffs include the total absence of onboard storage and hardware accelerators, limiting its utility for massive datasets residing strictly in memory or deep learning acceleration. Best-fit use cases include high-performance compute tasks, batch processing, CPU-bound scientific modeling, distributed compilation, and highly scaled web service layers.

The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, delivering approximately 1.85 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included, and the instance provides no local disk storage, relying on external network storage solutions for data persistence. A 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth supports high-throughput data transfer across distributed environments. Cost efficiency stems from its high CPU density and dedicated core allocation, avoiding multi-tenant resource contention while prioritizing pure compute capacity over memory volume. The server is well suited for compute-intensive tasks, parallel batch processing, distributed software compilation, and large-scale CPU-driven simulations that do not require massive per-core memory or dedicated local NVMe storage.
